steps.title: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living organisms.
steps.body: In multicellular organisms, cells become specialised for particular functions. Similar cells group together to form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together in organ systems.

steps.title: Multicellular organisms
steps.body: are organised into a hierarchy: cells specialise, group into tissues, tissues combine into organs, and organs form organ systems. This allows large organisms to function efficiently.

steps.title: Animal tissues
steps.body: include muscular tissue (for movement), glandular tissue (for producing secretions), and epithelial tissue (for covering surfaces). Each tissue is made of cells specialised for its function.

steps.title: Remember
steps.body: These three tissues are found in the stomach. Muscular tissue churns food, glandular tissue produces digestive juices, and epithelial tissue lines the inside surface.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Define the term "tissue." (1 mark) | Describe the hierarchy of organisation in a multicellular organism. (4 marks) | Name the three types of tissue found in the stomach and state the function of each. (3 marks)

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A tissue is a group of similar cells with the same function working together. | Cells are the basic units and become specialised for particular functions. Similar specialised cells group together to form tissues. Different tissues combine to form organs. Organs work together in o | Muscular tissue - contracts to churn food; glandular tissue - produces digestive juices (enzymes and acid); epithelial tissue - lines the surface of the stomach.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the hierarchy in order: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism Do not confuse "tissue" and "organ" - a tissue has one cell type, an organ has multiple tissue types When asked about the stomach, always name the three tissues AND their functions For plant tissues, make sure you can explain WHY palisade cells have many chloroplasts (for photosynthesis) and WHY spongy mesophyll has air spaces (for gas exchange) Remember xylem transports water UP, phloem transports sugars in BOTH directions Questions often ask "Explain why X is an organ" - your answer must mention that it contains different tissues working together
